response:
Sure, here are the rules of disc golf:

1. There are three baskets on a circular course about 180 yards (165 feet) apart. These are called the “tees” on the course.

2. A disc player rolls their disc into the air, and bounces it off the front of the basket, then drops it into the hole.

3. Each basket has a flag attached to it. If a ball comes down the middle of the fairway, it’s a “pushpin” as opposed to a “push” which goes in the hole.

4. A “pin” is any ball that hits the ground after it’s landed in the ground and doesn’t return up again. Also, a “hole-in-one,” is when a player gets their disc into all three baskets. 

5. A player can only “spin” a disc while it is on the ground. This means they are allowed to make a turn with their disc. Once the disc is in the air, they are not allowed to make any turns with it. 

6. A player can pick up their disc and use it on another disc. They can also hold their disc in their hands. 

7. A player can also “roll” their disc while it is in the air. They do this by tapping their wrist on their disc and spinning their disc in the opposite direction.

8. A “three-putter” is a rule where a player can only three put their disc on each tee. If they do two more putts, they get a “one-putter”. The “putter” is the object on the course that the disc goes in. 

9. There are multiple hazards (sand dunes, trees) on the course that can cause the disc to bounce or turn sideways. A disc that turns sideways or lands on the inside of the fairway is called “flying” and should be considered a “push.” It’s rare, but happens.

10. There is a “tee off” where all players start their game on the same hole. This also means they all start the game from the “tee” basket on the course. When everyone is on their initial shot, they can “put” their disc on the next one to be played. 

11. A “putter on” is a rule where a player is given no more “putter” space from their own. The player who has this rule, is told they can only put their disc on the next hole. 

12. A “hole-in-one” is rare, but possible with some good shotmaking. If a player gets it on course, they win a medal. If a player gets it on a hole, they get a prize.

I hope that helps!
